data.name: Dragomir
data.gender_notes: Dragomir is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Slavic elements 'drag' meaning 'dear' or 'peace' and 'mir' meaning 'world' or 'peace'. This name signifies a peaceful, beloved one. The name Dragomir carries the meaning “Peace, Dear One” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Dragomir usually hope their child will grow to embody peace, dear one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of God's eternal love and peace in one's heart.
data.etymology: Dragomir belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Peace, Dear One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dragomir total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: דרגומיר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דרגומיר מורכב מהמילים 'דרג' - דרגה, עוצמה ומיר' - שליט, המתאר מישהו שהוא חזק, עוצמתי ושולט. השם נזכר בספרי השם-ישויות הבלארוסיות, והוא ידוע כשם נפוץ בקרב הכנסייה האורתודוקסית הבלארוסית. ברבות הימים, השם עבר לבשם דרגומיר, שהוא שם נפוץ בקרב התושבים הסלאבים. השם נשאר פופולרי בעיקר בחברה הכנסייתית של העיר רומניה.

in_greek.name: Δραγόμιρ
in_greek.meaning: αυτός που κατέχει δύναμη και δικαιοσύνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Δραγόμιρ προέρχεται από τις λέξεις 'δράγος' - δράκος, και 'μισός' - δίκαιος, και περιγράφει κάποιον που κατέχει δύναμη και δικαιοσύνη. Η λέξη 'δράγος' είναι αρχαία ελληνική λέξη που σημαίνει δράκος, ενώ η λέξη 'μισός' σημαίνει δίκαιος. Ο Δραγόμιρ ήταν ένα όνομα που χρησιμοποιούταν στη Δακία, μια περιοχή της Ρωμαϊκής Αυτοκρατορίας, την οποία αργότερα έγιναν γνωστές ως Ουγγαρία και Βοημία. Τα αρχαία Σλαβικά και Σλαβικών σλαβικών γλωσσών έχουν το ίδιο όνομα, και το χρησιμοποιούσαν για να περιγράψουν κάποιον που είναι δίκαιος και έχει δύναμη.

in_latin.name: Dragomir
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Dragomir a duabus Latinis verbis compositum est, 'draco' et 'mirus', et significat hominem qui virtutem et iustitiam habet. In antiquis Dacorum gentibus, nomen Dragomir erat commune, et significabat virum qui virtutem et iustitiam habet. Postea, nomen Dragomir in linguas Slavicam traduxit, et in multis gentibus Slavicis usum habebat. In Ecclesia Orthodoxa, nomen Dragomir adhuc usitatum est, et significat hominem qui virtutem et iustitiam habet.

in_english.name: Dragomir
in_english.meaning: holder of power and justice, strong and virtuous man
in_english.long_meaning: The name Dragomir is derived from the Slavic words 'drakon' meaning dragon and 'mir' meaning peace or world. In the Eastern European context, Dragomir is a name associated with strength, power, and virtuous character. The name Dragomir is of Slavic origin and is commonly found among the Orthodox Christian communities. It is believed to have originated in the medieval times when the Slavs were influenced by the Byzantine Empire. In modern times, the name Dragomir is associated with values such as power, strength, and justice.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dragomir had a significant impact on Slavic cultures. It was a common name in Eastern Europe, and many rulers and saints bore the name. For instance, there was a medieval ruler of Czech lands named Vratislav II, whose byname was Dragomir. This name implies a ruler who was beloved by his people and maintained peace in his kingdom.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Dragomir represents God's unwavering love and peace. "Drago" in the name could be interpreted as a unique expression of God's love for every individual, while "mir" conveys the sense of unity and peace that comes through that love. It can be seen as a reminder of God's promise to be with us through both good and challenging times, bringing peace and love to us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dragomir means "peace-loving" or "beloved peace" in Old Slavic. It reflects the Christian ideal of inner peace and harmony, as well as the importance of faith and love in fostering unity and tranquility.

historical_references.reference: Dragomir I (552-576 AD) was a ruler of the First Bulgarian State. He was the eldest son of Terbel, who was a regional leader in the Danube region. During his reign, he successfully resisted the Byzantine Emperor Justinian's attempts to conquer Bulgaria. Dragomir was also the first Christian ruler of Bulgaria and is believed to have been baptized by Pope Vigilius in 552 AD.

historical_references.reference: Dragomir (died 1241) was a voivode of Moldavia, ruling the region from 1236 to 1240 AD. He played an important role in the history of Moldavia during the Mongol invasion of Eastern Europe. Dragomir managed to repel the invading Mongol army and kept Moldavia independent. He is remembered as a courageous and successful military leader in the face of the Mongol threat.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Dragomir has seen a resurgence in modern culture, particularly in areas related to Romanian royalty, medieval history, and science fiction and fantasy. In the online game World of Warcraft, a character named Dragomir is a powerful mage who hails from the eastern kingdom of Kul Tiras. In the Assassin's Creed series, Dragomir is the name of a Romanian monk who is a mentor and ally to the protagonist. In romance novels, Dragomir is a common name for romantic heroes, often portrayed as strong, noble, and mysterious. Overall, the name Dragomir evokes a sense of history, power, and enchantment.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Grace Dragomir in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Dragomir, which means "Peace, Dear One". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
